plan: Reduce exposure to QQQI to 20% to lower concentration.
Eliminate all leveraged ETFs like SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, MSFU, and PLTU.
Focus on capital preservation by cutting high-risk positions.
This plan prioritizes stability and reduces overall portfolio risk.
A larger cash buffer will be maintained for safety.
conservative.read: This plan aims for capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and lowering concentration. Expect lower drawdowns but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration while keeping income exposure.
Reduce most leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU) to 1% each.
Sell SPAL entirely to cut high-risk leveraged exposure.
Add XLV as a new position at 4% for defensive sector diversification.
This plan balances growth with risk reduction, aiming for steady returns.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets approximately 2.5% monthly growth with a risk-first mindset. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a defensive sector. Expect moderate growth and controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration while retaining some income.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to 6% each.
Add XLV as a new position at 6% for diversification.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly growth by increasing leverage and concentrating in high-potential, albeit high-risk, assets. Be aware of amplified gains and losses, daily leveraged ETF decay, and the potential for substantial drawdowns.

plan: Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to maximize income generation.
Eliminate all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU, SPAL) to reduce volatility.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly income over capital appreciation.
Focus is on parking cash for yield with minimal risk.
Expect lower growth but more consistent distributions.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing capital preservation and steady cash flow. It cuts all leverage and high-beta single names. While distributions are variable, the goal is low drawdown and reliable income.
